dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 

Key Provisions
1.	Central Authority and National Jurisdiction
•	Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE): Established under Section 3, operating under central government oversight.
•	National Energy Efficiency Enforcement: Central Government's role in setting and enforcing national energy efficiency norms.
2.	State Jurisdiction and Powers
•	State-Level Enforcement: Under Section 15, states are empowered to enforce energy conservation within their territorial boundaries.
•	State Energy Conservation Fund: Each state manages its fund for local initiatives, highlighting decentralized financial authority.
3.	Shared and Overlapping Jurisdictions
4.	Designated Consumers and Energy Audits: While the designation of consumers is a national standard, the oversight and audit enforcement can involve both central and state authorities.
5.	Energy Efficiency Standards: National standards apply, but states may enforce additional, stricter regulations within their jurisdictions.
6.	Regulatory Framework Across Jurisdictions
•	Central Government Rules: Apply uniformly across India, covering national energy policies.
•	State Government Rules: Allow for tailored regulations to address local energy conservation needs.
7.	Bureau’s Regulations: Operate within the national framework, with potential for state-specific adaptations.

(1) No person shall occupy or encroach on any highway within the highway boundaries without obtaining the previous permission in writing of the Highway Authority or an officer authorized in this behalf by the Highway Authority.

(i) to place a temporary encroachment on any highway in front of any building owned by him or make a temporary structure overhanging the highway, or
(ii) to put up a temporary awning or tent, pandal or other similar erection or a temporary stall or scaffolding on any highway, or
(iii) to deposit or cause to be deposited building materials, goods for sale or other articles on any highway, or
(iv) to make a temporary excavation for carrying out any repairs or improvements to adjoining building :

(5) The Highway Authority or the officer issuing the permission shall maintain a complete record of all such permissions issued and shall also cause a check-up to be made in every case at the expiration of the period up to which occupation has been authorized to ensure that the land has actually been vacated.
